features.norm: Metadata streams may carry document/object metadata; Info carries document metadata. Metadata streams are preferred in PDF 2.0; Info use other than CreationDate/ModDate is deprecated. This constrains writers; it does not direct a reader to reject or ignore legacy Info.
features.assessment: both sources are read and public consumers preserve source distinction

features.norm: 14.1 says metadata does not affect final appearance; no required visual rendering follows from metadata alone.
features.evidence: Query::Properties and document-properties panel, not page painter
features.assessment: panel is a chosen informational surface; not a rendering requirement

features.norm: Metadata stream dictionary shall state /Type /Metadata and /Subtype /XML.
features.assessment: writer assertion exists; reader intentionally parses stream contents without requiring these writer-only tags

features.norm: Contents shall be XML and its grammar shall follow XMP ISO 16684-1; EC3 #296 adds that all XMP metadata in PDF shall be UTF-8.
features.evidence: pdf-model/src/xmp.rs parser, xmp.rs unit tests, corpus read gate; EC3 overlay transcribed at doc/errata-read.md:2733 (physical PDF p.730, printed footer p.715)
features.assessment: UTF-8 emitted output has a writer test; reader also accepts UTF-16/UTF-32 by BOM as deliberate extra tolerance, not a reader-duty failure

features.kind: producer structure and generic reader API
features.norm: Catalog Metadata carries document packet; Table 348 allows metadata on component stream/dictionary; marked-content property lists may also carry an indirect metadata stream named through resource properties.
features.evidence: Xmp::read accepts a dictionary; Xmp::document reads catalog; pdf-model/tests/xmp.rs::a_metadata_stream_on_a_form_xobject_reads_back
features.assessment: generic reading and object-carrier control exist; no in-scope display/use consumer is required for all object-level packets

features.norm: Metadata encryption follows Table 21 and §7.6, not a separate §14.3 behavior.

features.feature: document packet query and informational surface
features.norm: §14.3 does not mandate a properties panel or selection of properties to display; metadata is informational rather than page appearance.
features.evidence: viewer-core Query::Properties returns Information plus Option<Result<Xmp>>; viewer-host::panel::property_rows labels packet separately
features.assessment: public data route exists. Test gap: no property_rows assertion currently covers packet-bearing and conflicting Info/XMP title values side by side

features.norm: Info is optional; when present it holds a document information dictionary. PDF 2.0 deprecation is producer direction, not an instruction to discard extant data.
features.assessment: optional/no-Info control and table fields tested

features.norm: Six non-date entries other than Trapped are text strings; CreationDate/ModDate are date values; Trapped is a name True/False/Unknown, with Unknown default. ModDate is required if catalog PieceInfo is present.
features.evidence: metadata.rs::in_dictionary and table_349 test; metadata_requirements_audit tests conditional ModDate; xmp/transform writer tests
features.assessment: non-string title and boolean Trapped controls exist; parser date mechanics excluded from this shard per assignment

features.norm: Info dictionaries are also used with Threads; reader API supports a held dictionary.
features.assessment: support exists; no new test need identified in bounded crosscut review

features.title: Reconciling two sources of document metadata

features.feature: date equivalence when writing creation/last-modification values
features.norm: First creation dates and last-modification dates shall be fully equivalent across Info and document XMP if both are written; an existing inconsistent creation pair should remain unchanged on modification; a missing counterpart may be added if equivalent.
features.evidence: pdf-transform update.rs earlier-version test and merge.rs date-equivalence test; archive metadata conversion; ADR 1473
features.assessment: existing writer tests compare both date representations. Date parser itself not reassessed

features.norm: If inconsistent created/modified date values are encountered, use is at PDF processor discretion.
features.evidence: metadata panel renders Info and XMP under separate labeled headings; writer tests enforce equivalence only when writing both
features.assessment: showing both separately is a defensible product policy; no standard-mandated precedence exists here

features.norm: §14.3.4 rules concern creation and modification time/date, not all Table 349/XMP counterpart values. Table NOTE counterparts do not create a general reader reconciliation rule.
features.evidence: EC3 effective §14.3.4 printed p.718; Table 349 pp.716–717
features.assessment: do not infer a requirement to merge or choose between conflicting titles/authors in Properties panel

remaining_work: No general ISO 16684-1 XMP validator certification is claimed; this pass inspected reader paths needed by §14.3 consumers and relevant tests only.
Date parsing/normalization behavior was assigned to a prior audit and is not revisited here; only existing writer consistency assertions were mapped.
The new panel test is product-regression coverage, not a standard-required source precedence behavior.
Object-level metadata can be decoded from a held dictionary; this pass found no in-scope consumer duty to display every object packet.
